items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: a lot of great names — the Hackney brothers that played with, they both played with Dizzy didn’t they?

ctx.x: Well, just for the archive, Sam is older than me, and by the time I was starting to get into music and starting to play, Sam was already on the scene, and I wasn’t old enough to get into a lot of clubs, and he was just past the age limit so I used to hear him play like at the — the first time I saw him really was at The Flamingo on Delaware Avenue, Delaware and Tupper — Chippewa. And I remember seeing him and Larry Covelli, also another great saxophonist from — jazz saxophone player from Buffalo, New York. And…

But it was a place to go play. Sunday afternoon jazz sessions, I mean sessions where you could play and you used to have to go in and almost sign up backstage and get in line and wait to play. And everybody was very — I mean so far as I was concerned — everybody was very encouraging to help me play and learn how to play, and a lot of great names — the Hackney brothers that played with, they both played with Dizzy didn’t they?
